images.title: The multiply rule
images.purpose: Show that 4/6 and 6/9 come from 2/3 by multiplying the numerator and the denominator by the same number.
images.composition: Three large fractions in a row with wide gaps, and two curved arrows from the first fraction to the other two.
images.exact_structure: Left: the large fraction 2/3 in teal #0072B2. Middle: the large fraction 4/6 in amber #E69F00. Right: the large fraction 6/9 in amber #E69F00. One reddish purple #CC79A7 curved arrow goes over the top from 2/3 to 4/6, with its label above it. A second reddish purple curved arrow goes underneath from 2/3 to 6/9, with its label below it. A short caption is centred at the bottom. Exactly 3 fractions and 2 arrows.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a plus sign anywhere on an arrow, or any number other than 2 and 3 as a multiplier
images.takeaway: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number to get an equivalent fraction.
images.description: 2/3 with one arrow to 4/6 marked × 2 top and bottom and one arrow to 6/9 marked × 3 top and bottom; all three are equivalent fractions.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to follow each arrow and say what the top and the bottom of 2/3 were both multiplied by.

image_decisions.why: The multiply rule is a pattern that one clean arrow picture makes easy to spot.
